subject: general
question: A metallic sphere of unknown radius is melted and recast into 64 smaller spherical balls. During the recasting process, 20% of the total metal is lost as waste. If the total volume of the 64 smaller spheres after the loss is 10,752 cm³, determine the radius (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the original sphere. (Use pi = 3.14 )
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Final volume = 10752 cm³ represents 80% of original metal

Original volume = 10752 ÷ 0.8 = 13440 cm³

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

13440 = (4/3) × 3.14 × r³

r³ ≈ 3213

**∴ r ≈ 15 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total volume of 64 small spheres after loss = 10752 cm³

Loss = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Remaining metal = 80% of original

⇒ Original volume = 10752 ÷ 0.8 = 13440 cm³

⇒ Using formula:

⇒ 13440 = (4/3) × 3.14 × r³

⇒ 13440 = 4.1867 × r³

⇒ r³ = 13440 ÷ 4.1867 ≈ 3210

⇒ r ≈ ∛3210 ≈ 15 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Sphere

Volume = (4/3)πr³

Percentage Loss

If x% is lost, remaining = (100 − x)% of original

Recasting Concept

Total volume is conserved except for loss during melting
